mainTopic: Harmful spirits, where the שכינה rests, and God's תפילין
overview: This amud starts by finishing an earlier topic: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא says that someone who waits in the בית כנסת for his friend to finish praying earns the blessings of a פסוק in ישעיהו. Then אבא בנימין, אביי, רב הונא and רבא describe the countless מזיקין around us and the everyday troubles they cause. The גמרא gives a way to detect them and a way to see them, and tells how רב ביבי בר אביי was harmed after trying it. Next, אבא בנימין teaches that prayer is truly heard in the בית כנסת. רבי יצחק adds that the שכינה is with ten who pray, three who judge, two who learn, and even one who learns, and the גמרא explains what each larger group gains. Along the way רב אשי teaches that a מצוה someone planned but was forced to miss counts as if he did it. Finally, רבי יצחק teaches that God wears תפילין, which contain praise of ישראל such as 'Who is like Your people ישראל, one nation in the land'. The amud ends by showing how these פסוקים fit into four compartments.

steps.title: The reward for waiting for a friend who is still praying
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא says that one who waits for his friend to finish praying earns the blessings listed in ישעיהו 48:18–19.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: He earns these blessings, as the פסוק says: 'If only you had listened to My commandments, your peace would be like a river, and your righteousness like the waves of the sea. Your children would be like the sand, and the offspring of your body...' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers a question raised just before this: what reward does a person get for waiting for his friend to finish praying? רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא answers with a פסוק full of blessings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just before this, the גמרא taught that leaving while a friend is still praying is wrong, and then asked what the reward is for waiting. רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא says the person gets the blessings in this פסוק: peace like a river, righteousness like the sea's waves, and many children. The גמרא does not explain here exactly how the פסוק connects to waiting. It just brings it as the source.

keyTerms.meaning: as it is said (introduces a פסוק)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that staying with a friend so he is not left alone while praying is an act that earns great reward.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Ḥanina said:
He merits these blessings,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the person who waited for his friend to finish praying. That is the question the גמרא just asked.

phrases.english: as it is said: 'If only you had listened to My commandments,'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 48:18–19

phrases.english: then your peace would be like a river,
and your righteousness like the waves of the sea.
Your children would be like the sand,
and the offspring of your body...' and so on.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא: זוֹכֶה לַבְּרָכוֹת הַלָּלוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised just before this part: what is the reward for waiting for a friend who is still praying.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who waits for his friend to finish praying earns the blessings of ישעיהו 48:18–19.
steps.whatToRemember: Waiting for your friend to finish praying earns the blessings of peace, righteousness and many children from the פסוק in ישעיהו.

steps.title: If our eyes could see the harmful spirits
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes אבא בנימין: if the eye could see the מזיקין, no creature could bear to stand before them.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: אבא בנימין says: If the eye were allowed to see, no creature could stand up in front of the harmful spirits.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new subject, the מזיקין (harmful spirits). It brings a ברייתא from אבא בנימין saying that they are all around us but hidden from our eyes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבא בנימין says the only reason we can live calmly is that we cannot see the מזיקין. If we could see how many there are, no one could stand it. The next two statements will explain just how many there are.

keyTerms.meaning: if only / if it were so that

phrases.english: It was taught: Abba Binyamin says:
If permission were given
to the eye to see,
no creature would be able
to stand before the harmful spirits.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אַבָּא בִּנְיָמִין אוֹמֵר: אִלְמָלֵי נִתְּנָה רְשׁוּת לָעַיִן לִרְאוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, another teaching of אבא בנימין, this time about מזיקין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מזיקין are so many that if we could see them, no one could bear it.

steps.title: אביי: They outnumber us and surround us
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the מזיקין are more numerous than people and surround us like the mounds of dirt around a dug pit.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: They are more than us, and they stand around us like the piled-up earth around a pit.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds to אבא בנימין's teaching by describing how many מזיקין there are and how close they are to us.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבא בנימין said we could not bear to see them. אביי explains why: there are more of them than of us, and they crowd around us. He compares it to the dirt piled up all around the edge of a freshly dug pit.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
They are more numerous than we are,
and they stand around us
like the earth piled around a pit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: אִינְהוּ נְפִישִׁי מִינַּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports and adds detail to אבא בנימין's statement about the מזיקין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מזיקין outnumber people and surround them closely.

steps.title: רב הונא: A thousand on the left, ten thousand on the right
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא gives numbers: every person has a thousand מזיקין on his left and ten thousand on his right.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: Every single one of us has a thousand on his left and ten thousand on his right.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא continues the same topic and puts numbers on how many מזיקין surround each person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said they are more than us. רב הונא makes it concrete and personal: each person, not just people in general, has a thousand on one side and ten thousand on the other. This finishes the series of statements about how many מזיקין there are.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
Each and every one of us has
a thousand on his left
phrases.notes: The numbers match תהלים 91:7: 'A thousand may fall at your side, and ten thousand at your right.'

phrases.english: and ten thousand on his right.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: כֹּל חַד וְחַד מִינַּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds exact numbers to אביי's general statement that the מזיקין outnumber us.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each person is surrounded by a thousand מזיקין on the left and ten thousand on the right.
steps.whatToRemember: אבא בנימין: we could not bear to see the מזיקין. אביי: they outnumber us and surround us. רב הונא: a thousand on each person's left and ten thousand on his right.

steps.title: Everyday troubles that come from the harmful spirits
steps.stepSummary: רבא lists four common problems, such as crowding at the כלה gathering and worn-out clothes of תלמידי חכמים, and says they are caused by the מזיקין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The crowding at the כלה gathering comes from the מזיקין. Knees that feel tired come from them. The clothes of the Rabbis that wear out come from rubbing against them. Legs that get bruised come from them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא takes the idea from the earlier steps, that we are surrounded by huge numbers of מזיקין, and points to everyday effects of this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous steps said the מזיקין are everywhere but invisible. רבא now explains ordinary things we do notice, like crowding, tiredness, and worn clothing, as the hidden result of their presence. It turns an abstract claim into something you can see in daily life.

keyTerms.meaning: The large gatherings for Torah learning held in the months of אֱלוּל and אֲדָר

phrases.english: Rava said:
This crowding that happens at the kalla gathering
phrases.notes: The כלה was the big learning gathering where crowds came to hear Torah.

phrases.english: comes from them.
phrases.notes: "Them" means the מזיקין from the earlier steps.

phrases.english: Those knees that are tired come from them.
Those clothes of the Rabbis that wear out
come from rubbing against them.
Those legs that get bruised come from them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הַאי דּוּחְקָא דְּהָוֵי בְּכַלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of the many מזיקין around us by showing their everyday effects.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Crowding at the כלה, tired knees, worn-out clothes of the Rabbis, and bruised legs are all caused by the מזיקין.

steps.title: How to find signs that the spirits are there
steps.stepSummary: Someone who wants proof that מזיקין exist should spread fine ash around his bed, and in the morning he will see tracks like chicken feet.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whoever wants to know about them should take fine ash and spread it around his bed. In the morning he will see marks like the feet of a chicken.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a simple test to detect the מזיקין, even though they cannot be seen directly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the eye cannot see the מזיקין (step 2), this method lets a person see their footprints instead. It shows evidence of them without seeing them.

phrases.english: One who wants to know about them
should bring fine ash,
and spread it around his bed,
and in the morning he sees
marks like the feet of a chicken.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי מַאן דְּבָעֵי לְמִידַּע לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from describing the effects of the מזיקין to a way of detecting them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fine ash spread around the bed will show chicken-like footprints of the מזיקין in the morning.

steps.title: How to actually see the spirits, and how to stay safe
steps.stepSummary: A method for seeing the מזיקין using the burned afterbirth of a special black cat, plus instructions to lock the powder away so the spirits cannot steal it and harm him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whoever wants to see them should take the afterbirth of a black female cat, born to a black female cat, a firstborn born to a firstborn. He should burn it in fire, grind it, and fill his eyes with it, and then he will see them. He should put it in an iron tube and seal it with an iron seal, because they might steal it from him. And he should seal its opening, so that he will not be harmed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes one step further than the ash test and gives a way to actually see the מזיקין, along with safety instructions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 2 said that if the eye could see them, no one could stand it. Here we learn there is a way to see them, but it comes with danger, so the powder must be locked in iron. This prepares us for the next story, which shows that this danger is real.

phrases.english: One who wants to see them,
should bring the afterbirth of a black female cat
born to a black female cat,
a firstborn born to a firstborn,
and burn it in fire, and grind it,
and fill his eyes with it, and he will see them.
And he should put it in an iron tube,
phrases.notes: "It" is the leftover ground powder.

phrases.english: and seal it with an iron seal,
because they might steal it from him,
and he should seal its opening,
so that he will not be harmed.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי מַאן דְּבָעֵי לְמֶחֱזִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes beyond detecting their footprints to a method of actually seeing the מזיקין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Putting the burned and ground afterbirth of a firstborn black cat into one's eyes lets one see the מזיקין, and the powder must be sealed in iron to prevent harm.

steps.title: The story of רב ביבי בר אביי, who tried it and was harmed
steps.stepSummary: רב ביבי בר אביי did this method, saw the מזיקין, and was harmed, and he was healed only after the Rabbis prayed for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ביבי בר אביי did this. He saw them and was harmed. The Rabbis prayed for mercy for him, and he was healed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story showing what happened when someone actually used the method from the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story proves that seeing the מזיקין really is dangerous, just as step 2 warned. Even a great רבי was harmed and needed the prayers of others to be healed.
steps.whatToRemember: The מזיקין are everywhere and cause everyday troubles; trying to see them is dangerous, as the story of רב ביבי בר אביי shows.

phrases.aramaic: רַב בִּיבִי בַּר אַבָּיֵי עֲבַד הָכִי,
phrases.english: Rav Beivai bar Abaye did this,
he saw them and was harmed,
the Rabbis prayed for mercy for him, and he was healed.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב בִּיבִי בַּר אַבָּיֵי עֲבַד הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A real-life story showing the danger of the method described in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Seeing the מזיקין caused real harm, healed only through the prayers of the Rabbis.

steps.title: Prayer is truly heard in the synagogue
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes אבא בנימין: a person's prayer is heard only in a בית הכנסת, learned from a פסוק that links prayer to the place of song.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: אבא בנימין says: A person's prayer is heard only in a בית הכנסת, as it says: "To listen to the song and to the prayer." In the place of song, there prayer should be.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the topic of מזיקין and returns to prayer, bringing another teaching of אבא בנימין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts "song" and "prayer" side by side. אבא בנימין reads this to mean that prayer belongs where songs of praise to ה׳ are sung, which is the בית הכנסת. That is the place where prayer is really heard.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean prayer anywhere else is worthless. It means the בית הכנסת is the place where prayer is heard in the fullest way.

phrases.english: It was taught: Abba Binyamin says:
A person's prayer is not heard
except in the synagogue,
as it says: "To listen to the song and to the prayer."
phrases.notes: מלכים א 8:28

phrases.english: In the place of song, there prayer should be.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אַבָּא בִּנְיָמִין אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Switches from the topic of מזיקין back to the theme of prayer from step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person's prayer is heard only in the בית הכנסת, the place where songs of praise are sung.

steps.title: ה׳ is found in the synagogue
steps.stepSummary: רבין בר רב אדא quotes רבי יצחק: we know הקדוש ברוך הוא is present in the בית הכנסת from the פסוק "God stands in the congregation of God."
steps.simpleTranslation: רבין בר רב אדא said in the name of רבי יצחק: How do we know that הקדוש ברוך הוא is found in the בית הכנסת? As it says: "God stands in the congregation of God."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching with a פסוק that shows ה׳'s presence is in the בית הכנסת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The "congregation of God" is a gathering of Jews coming together to serve ה׳, as in the בית הכנסת. The פסוק says ה׳ "stands" there. This helps explain why prayer is best heard in the בית הכנסת, as the previous step taught.
steps.whyThisMatters: Together with step 9, this gives the basis for the great importance of praying in a בית הכנסת: it is where ה׳'s presence is found.
steps.whatToRemember: Prayer is heard in the fullest way in the בית הכנסת, because that is where הקדוש ברוך הוא is present among the congregation.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבִין בַּר רַב אַדָּא, אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Ravin bar Rav Adda said that Rabbi Yitzchak said:
From where do we know that the Holy One, Blessed be He,
is found in the synagogue?
As it says: "God stands in the congregation of God."
phrases.notes: תהלים 82:1. The "congregation" is a group of Jews gathered together, as in a בית הכנסת.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבִין בַּר רַב אַדָּא, אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: מִנַּיִן שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מָצוּי בְּבֵית הַכְּנֶסֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a source showing ה׳ is present in the בית הכנסת, which supports why prayer is heard there.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הקדוש ברוך הוא is present in the בית הכנסת, learned from "God stands in the congregation of God."

steps.title: The שכינה is with ten people who pray
steps.stepSummary: The same פסוק, 'God stands in the congregation of God,' teaches that the שכינה is with a group of ten who pray together.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know that when ten people pray, the שכינה is with them? Because it says: 'God stands in the congregation of God.'
steps.whatsHappening: The teaching from step 10 continues. Now the same פסוק is used to show that the שכינה is with any group of ten people who pray together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 10 the פסוק proved that הקדוש ברוך הוא is in the בית הכנסת. Here the focus moves from the place to the people: ten people praying together. The word עדה ('congregation') is understood as a group of at least ten.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know? (asking for a source)

phrases.english: And from where do we know that ten who pray
that the Divine Presence is with them?
As it says: "God stands in the congregation of God."
phrases.notes: תהלים 82:1. Here a 'congregation' (עדה) means at least ten people.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִנַּיִן לַעֲשָׂרָה שֶׁמִּתְפַּלְּלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי יצחק's teaching, using the same פסוק from step 10 for a group of ten who pray.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ten people praying together have the שכינה with them.

steps.title: The שכינה is with three judges
steps.stepSummary: The second half of the same פסוק, 'in the midst of the judges He judges,' teaches that the שכינה is with three judges sitting in a בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know that when three people sit as judges, the שכינה is with them? Because it says: 'In the midst of the judges He judges.'
steps.whatsHappening: The list continues with a smaller group: three judges. The proof comes from the second half of the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the word אלהים is read as 'judges,' not 'God.' Since a בית דין has at least three judges, the פסוק shows that God is present among three people judging.
steps.confusionAlert: In this פסוק the word אלהים means 'judges,' not God. That is why it can be about a בית דין.

phrases.english: And from where do we know that three who sit in judgment
that the Divine Presence is with them?
As it says: "In the midst of the judges He judges."
phrases.notes: This is the end of the same פסוק, תהלים 82:1. Here אלהים means 'judges.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִנַּיִן לִשְׁלֹשָׁה שֶׁיּוֹשְׁבִין בַּדִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern as step 11, moving down from ten people to three.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three judges sitting in judgment have the שכינה with them.

steps.title: The שכינה is with two people learning תורה
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק in מלאכי teaches that when two God-fearing people speak words of תורה together, God listens, so the שכינה is with them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know that when two people sit and learn תורה, the שכינה is with them? Because it says: 'Then those who feared ה׳ spoke to one another, and ה׳ listened,' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The list goes down to just two people learning תורה together. The proof is a פסוק saying God listens when two God-fearing people speak to each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'One to another' shows there are two people. 'ה׳ listened' shows that God is paying attention to them, meaning the שכינה is there. The end of this פסוק sets up the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: And so on (the rest of the פסוק)

phrases.english: And from where do we know that two who sit
and learn Torah, that the Divine Presence is with them?
As it says: "Then those who feared the Lord spoke

phrases.aramaic: אִישׁ אֶל רֵעֵהוּ וַיַּקְשֵׁב ה׳״ וְגוֹ׳.
phrases.english: one to another, and the Lord listened," and so on.
phrases.notes: מלאכי 3:16. The פסוק ends with 'and for those who think of His name,' which the next step asks about.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִנַּיִן לִשְׁנַיִם שֶׁיּוֹשְׁבִין וְעוֹסְקִין בַּתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern again, moving down from three to two.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two people learning תורה together have the שכינה with them.

steps.title: What does 'those who think of His name' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא stops on a phrase at the end of the פסוק from מלאכי and asks what it means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the meaning of 'and for those who think of His name'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses the list to ask about a phrase in the פסוק it just quoted. This sets up רב אשי's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק already mentions people who fear ה׳, so 'those who think of His name' seems to add something. The גמרא wants to know what extra group or idea this phrase is teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who think of His name

phrases.english: What is "and for those who think of His name"?
phrases.notes: These words come at the end of the same פסוק in מלאכי, which the גמרא shortened with 'and so on.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״וּלְחֹשְׁבֵי שְׁמוֹ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up a phrase from the פסוק quoted in step 13 and asks for its meaning.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the phrase 'those who think of His name' in מלאכי 3:16.

steps.title: רב אשי: a planned מצוה that was blocked counts as done
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that if someone planned to do a מצוה and was forced by circumstances not to do it, the פסוק counts it as if he did it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: If a person planned to do a מצוה, and something beyond his control stopped him, and he did not do it, the פסוק counts it for him as if he had done it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the question from step 14. 'Thinking of His name' means planning a מצוה, and God gives credit even when the plan was blocked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase is read as being about a person's thoughts. Someone who sincerely planned a מצוה but was stopped by אונס (being forced) still gets credit as if he did it. Both conditions matter: he really planned it, and something outside his control stopped him.

keyTerms.meaning: He was forced or stopped by circumstances beyond his control
The פסוק counts it for him

steps.whatToRemember: A sincere plan to do a מצוה that was blocked by אונס is counted as if it were done.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not about someone who just changed his mind or was lazy. The credit is for someone who really meant to do it and was stopped by something outside his control.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a well-known principle: God values a sincere intention to do a מצוה, even when the person could not carry it out.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
If a person intended to do a מצוה,
and was prevented by circumstances beyond his control, and did not do it,
the verse credits him
as if he had done it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: חָשַׁב אָדָם לַעֲשׂוֹת מִצְוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14 directly.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Those who think of His name' are people who planned a מצוה but were stopped by אונס; the פסוק counts it as if they did it.

steps.title: Even one person learning has the שכינה
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק in שמות teaches that the שכינה is with even a single person learning תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know that even one person who sits and learns תורה has the שכינה with him? Because the פסוק says: 'In every place where I cause My Name to be mentioned, I will come to you and bless you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds the last item to the list: even one person learning alone has the שכינה with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After ten, three and two, the list now goes down to one. The proof is a פסוק that speaks to 'you' in the singular, promising that God comes and blesses wherever His Name is mentioned. This finished list sets up the questions that come next.

keyTerms.meaning: I will cause My Name to be mentioned

phrases.english: And from where do we know that even one person
who sits and learns Torah
has the Divine Presence with him?

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״בְּכָל הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר אַזְכִּיר אֶת שְׁמִי
phrases.english: As it says: "In every place where I cause My Name to be mentioned
phrases.notes: שמות 20:21

phrases.english: I will come to you and bless you."
phrases.notes: The 'you' here is singular, so the פסוק is talking to just one person.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִנַּיִן שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list of groups (ten, three, two) by adding a single person.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שכינה is with even one person who learns תורה.

steps.title: If even one person has the שכינה, why mention two?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the list needed to mention two if even one person already gets the שכינה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But since even one person has the שכינה, why did we need to say two?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the list. If one is enough, saying 'two' seems extra. It is setting up an answer that will show what is special about two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is simple: if the smaller group already gets the שכינה, the bigger group obviously does too. So the list must be teaching something extra about two, and the גמרא wants to know what.

phrases.english: But since even one person has the Divine Presence,
was it necessary to say two?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מֵאַחַר דַּאֲפִילּוּ חַד, תְּרֵי מִבַּעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the new one-person teaching to question the two-person teaching.
steps.kashyaTarget: The teaching from step 13 that the שכינה is with two people.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the smaller group (one) gets the שכינה, the larger group (two) does too, so saying it seems extra.

steps.title: Two have their words written in the book of remembrance
steps.stepSummary: Two people learning together have their words written in the book of remembrance. One person alone does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: With two, their words are written in the book of remembrance. With one, his words are not written in the book of remembrance.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that two people get something extra: their תורה words are written in the book of remembrance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both one and two have the שכינה, but the פסוק in מלאכי adds that a book of remembrance is written for people who speak to each other. That extra reward belongs only to two or more, so mentioning two was needed.

phrases.english: Two: their words are written
in the book of remembrance,
phrases.notes: This comes from the same פסוק in מלאכי from step 13: 'and a book of remembrance was written.'

phrases.english: one: his words are not written
in the book of remembrance.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּרֵי — מִכַּתְבָן מִלַּיְיהוּ בְּסֵפֶר הַזִּכְרוֹנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to an extra reward that only the larger group gets.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Two get nothing more than one, so mentioning two is extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two get an added reward: their words are written in the book of remembrance.

steps.title: If even two have the שכינה, why mention three?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the list mentioned three judges if even two people already get the שכינה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But since even two have the שכינה, why did we need to say three?
steps.whatsHappening: The same question comes back one level up: why mention the three judges? This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is the same reasoning as before. If two get the שכינה, three surely do, so the case of three judges in a בית דין must be teaching something new.

phrases.english: But since even two have the Divine Presence,
was it necessary to say three?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מֵאַחַר דַּאֲפִילּוּ תְּרֵי, תְּלָתָא מִבַּעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the same kind of challenge, now aimed at the three judges.
steps.kashyaTarget: The teaching from step 12 that the שכינה is with three judges.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If two get the שכינה, three surely do, so saying it seems extra.

steps.title: Judging is also תורה
steps.stepSummary: We might have thought judging is only about keeping peace and does not bring the שכינה. The case of three teaches that judging is also תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: judging is just about keeping peace, and the שכינה does not come. So it teaches us that judging is also תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the three judges were mentioned to teach that sitting in judgment counts as learning תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without this teaching, we might think a בית דין is only a practical tool for settling fights between people, not real תורה, and so not a place for the שכינה. Listing three judges shows that judging is itself תורה, so the שכינה comes there too.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (a mistaken first thought)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that ruling on everyday money fights in a בית דין is not just social work. It counts as learning תורה.

phrases.english: You might have said:
judging is just for keeping peace,
and so the Divine Presence does not come,
so it teaches us
that judging is also Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: דִּינָא שְׁלָמָא בְּעָלְמָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the case teaches a new idea: what counts as תורה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Judging is only about keeping peace, so the שכינה does not come.
steps.terutzMaskana: Judging is also תורה, so the שכינה comes.

steps.title: If even three have the שכינה, why mention ten?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the list mentioned ten if even three already get the שכינה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But since even three have the שכינה, why did we need to say ten?
steps.whatsHappening: The last round of the same question: why mention ten people praying together? This sets up the final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again, the bigger group seems to be covered by the smaller one. So mentioning ten must be teaching something extra.

phrases.english: But since even three have the Divine Presence,
was it necessary to say ten?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מֵאַחַר דַּאֲפִילּוּ תְּלָתָא, עֲשָׂרָה מִבַּעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the same kind of challenge, now aimed at the group of ten.
steps.kashyaTarget: The teaching from step 11 that the שכינה is with ten who pray.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If three get the שכינה, ten surely do, so saying it seems extra.

steps.title: For ten the שכינה comes first; for three only once they sit
steps.stepSummary: With ten, the שכינה is already there before they arrive. With three judges, it comes only once they sit down to judge.
steps.simpleTranslation: With ten, the שכינה comes first, before them. With three, it comes only once they sit down.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that ten are special because the שכינה gets there before them. For three judges, it comes only after they sit down to judge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference is not whether the שכינה comes but when. For ten, the פסוק says God 'stands' in the congregation, so He is there waiting. For judges, He comes 'in the midst' of their judging, after they begin.
steps.whatToRemember: Every group, even one person alone, has the שכינה, but each larger group gets something extra. Two have their words written in the book of remembrance. Three show that judging is תורה. For ten, the שכינה arrives before them.

phrases.english: Ten: the Divine Presence comes first, ahead of them.
Three: only once they sit down.
phrases.notes: He means the three judges from step 12. The שכינה comes only after they sit down to judge.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֲשָׂרָה — קָדְמָה שְׁכִינָה וְאָתְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 21 and closes the whole run of questions.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a difference in timing: when the שכינה arrives.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Ten get nothing more than three, so mentioning ten is extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: For ten the שכינה is there before them. For three it comes only once they sit to judge.

steps.title: God wears תפילין: the source
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק teaches that the הקדוש ברוך הוא wears תפילין, and brings a פסוק as the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבין בר רב אדא said in the name of רבי יצחק: How do we know that the הקדוש ברוך הוא puts on תפילין? Because the פסוק says, 'ה׳ swore by His right hand and by the arm of His strength.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new teaching: God Himself wears תפילין. It gives a פסוק as the source, and the next step will explain how the פסוק shows this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is a פסוק about God swearing by His right hand and His strong arm. On its own, the פסוק does not mention תפילין yet. The next step explains each part of the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know? (asking for a source)
The Holy One, Blessed be He (God)

steps.confusionAlert: This is אגדה describing God in human terms. It does not mean God has a body. It teaches something about God's bond with ישראל.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אָבִין בַּר רַב אַדָּא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Avin bar Rav Adda said,
Rabbi Yitzchak said:

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִן שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מַנִּיחַ תְּפִילִּין
phrases.english: From where do we know that the Holy One, Blessed be He, puts on tefillin?
As it says: "ה׳ swore by His right hand
and by the arm of His strength."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 62:8

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אָבִין בַּר רַב אַדָּא, אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: מִנַּיִן שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מַנִּיחַ תְּפִילִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new אגדה teaching, separate from the discussion of where the שכינה rests.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הקדוש ברוך הוא wears תפילין, as shown by the פסוק 'נשבע ה׳ בימינו ובזרוע עוזו'.

steps.title: Reading the פסוק: right hand is תורה, strong arm is תפילין
steps.stepSummary: Each half of the פסוק is explained with another פסוק: 'right hand' is the תורה and 'arm of His strength' is תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'His right hand' means the תורה, because the פסוק says 'From His right hand, a fiery law for them.' 'The arm of His strength' means תפילין, because the פסוק says 'ה׳ will give strength to His people.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the פסוק from the last step proves that God wears תפילין. It links each phrase to a different פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Right hand' is tied to the תורה, which was given 'from His right hand.' 'Strength' (עז) is tied to תפילין, through a פסוק that says God gives עז to His people. So God's 'arm of strength' is His תפילין. The next steps prove that תפילין are called 'strength'.

keyTerms.meaning: He will give to His people

phrases.english: "By His right hand" — this is the Torah,
as it says: "From His right hand, a fiery law for them,"
phrases.notes: דברים 33:2

phrases.english: "And by the arm of His strength" — these are tefillin,
as it says: "ה׳ will give strength to His people."
phrases.notes: תהלים 29:11. The link is the shared word עז, 'strength.'

steps.triggerLanguage: ״בִּימִינוֹ״ — זוֹ תּוֹרָה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the פסוק quoted in step 23 proves that God wears תפילין.
steps.raayaObject: That 'the arm of His strength' in the פסוק means תפילין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: 'מימינו אש דת למו' (דברים 33:2) for תורה, and 'ה׳ עז לעמו יתן' (תהלים 29:11) for תפילין.

steps.title: How do we know תפילין are strength for ישראל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source that תפילין count as 'strength' for ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know that תפילין are strength for ישראל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to check a link in the last step. It is setting up the next step, which will give the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last step assumed that 'strength' in 'ה׳ עז לעמו יתן' means תפילין. That needs proof, so the גמרא asks for it.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do we know?

phrases.english: And from where do we know that tefillin are strength for Israel?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִנַּיִן שֶׁהַתְּפִילִּין עוֹז הֵם לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for proof of the link between עז and תפילין used in step 24.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that תפילין are a 'strength' for ישראל.

steps.title: The nations see God's name on ישראל and fear them
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק says the nations will see God's name on ישראל and fear them, and רבי אליעזר הגדול says this means the head תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'All the nations of the earth will see that ה׳'s name is called upon you, and they will fear you.' And a ברייתא teaches that רבי אליעזר הגדול said: this means the תפילין on the head.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by joining a פסוק with a ברייתא. Together they show that תפילין make the nations fear ישראל, and that is strength.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says something called by God's name is seen on ישראל and makes the nations afraid. רבי אליעזר הגדול identifies it as the head תפילין. So תפילין are a source of strength.

keyTerms.meaning: ה׳'s name is called upon you
The תפילין worn on the head

steps.whatToRemember: תפילין are 'strength' for ישראל because the head תפילין show God's name on us, and the nations fear us because of it.

phrases.english: As it is written: "And all the nations of the earth will see
that the name of ה׳ is called upon you,
and they will fear you."
phrases.notes: דברים 28:10

phrases.english: And it was taught: Rabbi Eliezer the Great says:
These are the tefillin of the head.
phrases.notes: He means that the 'name of ה׳ upon you' that the nations see is the תפילין on the head.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: ״וְרָאוּ כׇּל עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ כִּי שֵׁם ה׳ נִקְרָא עָלֶיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'וראו כל עמי הארץ' together with רבי אליעזר הגדול's reading (it means the head תפילין) shows that תפילין make the nations fear ישראל.

steps.title: What is written in God's תפילין?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק asks רב חייא בר אבין what is written inside the תפילין of the Master of the world.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said to רב חייא בר אבין: These תפילין of the Master of the world, what is written in them?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know God wears תפילין, a new question comes up about what is inside them. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our תפילין hold parchments with פסוקים. If God wears תפילין, there must be something written in them too. רב נחמן בר יצחק asks what it is.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said to
Rav Chiya bar Avin:
These tefillin of the Master of the world,
what is written in them?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי תְּפִילִּין דְּמָרֵי עָלְמָא מָה כְּתִיב בְּהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 23's teaching that God wears תפילין and asks about what is inside them.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which words are written in God's תפילין.

steps.title: God's תפילין praise ישראל as one nation
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בר אבין answers that God's תפילין say: 'Who is like Your people ישראל, one nation in the land.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He answered him: 'And who is like Your people ישראל, one nation in the land?'
steps.whatsHappening: רב חייא בר אבין answers the question. God's תפילין contain a פסוק that praises ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our תפילין speak about God's oneness. God's תפילין speak about ישראל as one special nation. The answer shows how close and loving the bond between God and ישראל is.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is like Your people ישראל

steps.whatToRemember: God wears תפילין, and inside them is praise of ישראל: 'Who is like Your people ישראל, one nation in the land.'

phrases.english: He said to him:
"And who is like Your people Israel,
one nation in the land?"
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א 17:21

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ ״וּמִי כְּעַמְּךָ יִשְׂרָאֵל גּוֹי אֶחָד בָּאָרֶץ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: God's תפילין contain the פסוק 'ומי כעמך ישראל גוי אחד בארץ'.

steps.title: Is God praised through the praise of Israel?
steps.stepSummary: The conversation continues: is the קדוש ברוך הוא honored by having ישראל's praise written in His תפילין?
steps.simpleTranslation: Does God really take pride in the praises of ישראל?
steps.whatsHappening: Right after hearing that God's תפילין praise ישראל, the גמרא asks a follow-up: does God really glorify Himself through ישראל's praise? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our תפילין contain praise of God. It sounds strange that God's תפילין would contain praise of people. The question is how God could be glorified through praise of ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it really so that... (opens a question)
the Holy One, Blessed be He (Aramaic form)

phrases.english: And is the Holy One, Blessed be He, really praised
through the praises of Israel?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי מִשְׁתַּבַּח קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא בְּשִׁבְחַיְיהוּ דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follow-up question on the answer in step 28 about what God's תפילין say.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether, and how, God is glorified through praise of ישראל.

steps.title: Yes: Israel made God unique, and God makes Israel unique
steps.stepSummary: Two matching פסוקים show a two-way relationship: ישראל singles out God, and God singles out ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. One פסוק says 'You have affirmed the Lord today,' and the next says 'The Lord has affirmed you today.' God told ישראל: You made Me one special unit in the world, and I will make you one special unit in the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers yes. It brings two side-by-side פסוקים that use the same word (האמרת / האמירך) to show that God and ישראל single each other out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same word is used for what ישראל does for God and what God does for ישראל. That shows the relationship goes both ways. Because ישראל declares God unique, God declares ישראל unique, so their praise really is His glory.

keyTerms.meaning: you have affirmed / He has affirmed you (singled out and raised up)

phrases.english: Yes, as it is written:
"You have affirmed the Lord this day."
phrases.notes: דברים 26:17

phrases.english: And it is written: "And the Lord has affirmed you this day."
phrases.notes: דברים 26:18. It is the very next פסוק and uses the same word, so the two match each other.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְיִשְׂרָאֵל:
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Israel:
You have made Me one unique entity in the world,
phrases.notes: חטיבה means something singled out as one special unit, like a piece cut away on its own.

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲנִי אֶעֱשֶׂה אֶתְכֶם חֲטִיבָה אַחַת בָּעוֹלָם.
phrases.english: and I will make you one unique entity in the world.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין, דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. The paired פסוקים show a two-way bond: ישראל singles out God, and God singles out ישראל.

steps.title: The sources: שמע ישראל and גוי אחד בארץ
steps.stepSummary: Each half of God's statement is tied to a פסוק: ישראל calls God 'one' in שמע ישראל, and God calls ישראל 'one nation' in His תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'You made Me one unit' comes from 'Hear, Israel, the Lord is our God, the Lord is One.' 'I will make you one unit' comes from 'Who is like Your people Israel, one nation in the land.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows exactly where each side of the two-way bond is found in a פסוק. This ties the answer back to what is written in God's תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'one' (אחד) appears in both פסוקים. ישראל says God is אחד in שמע, which is written in our תפילין. God says ישראל is גוי אחד, which is written in His תפילין, so each side's תפילין praise the other.

keyTerms.meaning: as it is said (introduces a פסוק)
'Hear, Israel': the declaration of God's oneness

steps.whatToRemember: The bond is mirror-image: ישראל declares God 'אחד' (שמע ישראל, in our תפילין), and God declares ישראל 'גוי אחד' (in His תפילין).

phrases.english: You have made Me one unique entity in the world,
as it is said: "Hear, Israel,
the Lord is our God, the Lord is One."
phrases.notes: דברים 6:4

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲנִי אֶעֱשֶׂה אֶתְכֶם חֲטִיבָה אַחַת בָּעוֹלָם״,
phrases.english: And I will make you one unique entity in the world,
as it is said: "And who is like Your people Israel,
one nation in the land."

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתֶּם עֲשִׂיתוּנִי חֲטִיבָה אַחַת בָּעוֹלָם, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the פסוק behind each half of the statement in step 30.
steps.raayaObject: Each side of the 'one unique entity' statement.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמע ישראל (דברים 6:4) and ומי כעמך ישראל גוי אחד בארץ.

steps.title: What is in the other compartments?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא asks רב אשי: that פסוק fills one compartment of the head תפילין, so what is in the other compartments?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רבא said to רב אשי: That works for one compartment. What is in the other compartments?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question: head תפילין have four separate compartments, and so far we only know what is in one of God's. רב אחא בריה דרבא asks what fills the rest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our head תפילין have four boxes, each with its own passage praising God. If God's תפילין mirror ours, there must be four sets of praise of ישראל. Only one (גוי אחד בארץ) has been named so far.

keyTerms.meaning: that works out fine (for this part)
compartment / compartments (the boxes of head תפילין)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Acha, son of Rava, said to Rav Ashi:
That works out for one compartment,
phrases.notes: Literally 'one house'. He means one of the four little boxes in the head תפילין.

phrases.english: but in the other compartments, what is written?

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּינַח בְּחַד בֵּיתָא, בִּשְׁאָר בָּתֵּי מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 28's answer and asks to fill in the remaining compartments.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which praises of ישראל are written in the other compartments of God's head תפילין.

steps.title: More פסוקים praising Israel
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי lists five more פסוקים praising ישראל that are in the other compartments.
steps.simpleTranslation: He answered: 'For who is a great nation,' 'And who is a great nation,' 'Happy are you, Israel,' 'Or has God tried,' and 'And to make you high above.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers by naming the opening words of five פסוקים, each praising ישראל's special closeness to God. These fill the remaining compartments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the first פסוק ('Who is like Your people Israel'), each one praises ישראל as unique among nations. The list is not the final word, though: the next step points out that it has too many פסוקים for the compartments.
steps.confusionAlert: Five פסוקים are listed, but only three compartments are left. The next step raises exactly this problem, and step 35 solves it.
steps.whatToRemember: God's head תפילין mirror ours: ours praise God's oneness, and His praise ישראל's uniqueness in every compartment.

phrases.english: He said to him: "For who is a great nation,"
phrases.notes: דברים 4:7. He only quotes the first words of each פסוק.

phrases.english: "And who is a great nation,"
phrases.notes: דברים 4:8

phrases.english: "Happy are you, Israel,"
phrases.notes: דברים 33:29

phrases.english: "Or has God attempted,"
phrases.notes: דברים 4:34

phrases.english: "And to make you high above."
phrases.notes: דברים 26:19

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לֵיהּ: כִּי מִי גוֹי גָּדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 32's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The other compartments contain כי מי גוי גדול, ומי גוי גדול, אשריך ישראל, או הנסה אלהים, and ולתתך עליון.

steps.title: Too many פסוקים for the compartments
steps.stepSummary: If all those פסוקים are in the head תפילין, there would be more than four compartments.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, there are too many compartments!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב אשי's list. Head תפילין have only four compartments, but he listed more פסוקים than that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Head תפילין are built with four compartments, called בתים. Counting the one פסוק from before plus the five that רב אשי added gives more than four. So his list cannot fit if each פסוק gets its own compartment.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if what you said is true
Many compartments; more compartments than allowed
A compartment of the head תפילין (there are four)

phrases.english: If so,
phrases.notes: He means: if all the פסוקים רב אשי just listed are in the head תפילין.

phrases.english: there are too many compartments!
phrases.notes: Head תפילין have only four compartments, so this list won't fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, נְפִישִׁי לְהוּ טוּבֵי בָּתֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the list of פסוקים given in step 33.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's list of extra פסוקים in God's head תפילין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Head תפילין have exactly four compartments, but the list gives more than four פסוקים, so they can't each have their own compartment.

steps.title: Grouping the פסוקים into four compartments
steps.stepSummary: Similar פסוקים share a compartment, so the פסוקים fill exactly four compartments.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: 'For who is a great nation' and 'And who is a great nation,' which are similar to each other, are in one compartment. 'Happy are you, Israel' and 'Who is like Your people Israel' are in one compartment. 'Or has God tried' is in one compartment. 'And to make you high' is in one compartment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the problem by pairing up פסוקים that sound alike. Pairing them leaves exactly four compartments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two פסוקים that begin 'who is a great nation' share one compartment because they are worded alike. The two פסוקים that begin with 'Israel' praise share another. The last two פסוקים each get their own compartment, giving four in total.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; the גמרא is giving a corrected picture
That are similar to each other

steps.whatToRemember: God's head תפילין, like ours, have four compartments. Similar פסוקים praising ישראל are grouped together so they fit into exactly four.

phrases.english: Rather: "For who is a great nation"
phrases.notes: דברים 4:7

phrases.english: and "And who is a great nation," which are similar to each other,
phrases.notes: דברים 4:8. The two פסוקים sit right next to each other and start almost the same way.

phrases.english: are in one compartment;
"Happy are you, Israel" and "Who is like Your people Israel"
phrases.notes: דברים 33:29 and דברי הימים א 17:21.

phrases.english: are in one compartment;
"Or has God tried" is in one compartment;
phrases.notes: דברים 4:34

phrases.english: "And to make you high above" is in one compartment.
phrases.notes: דברים 26:19

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: כִּי מִי גוֹי גָּדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 34 by grouping the פסוקים.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reorganization: similar פסוקים share a compartment.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each פסוק would get its own compartment, which is too many.
steps.terutzMaskana: Pairs of similar פסוקים share a compartment, so there are exactly four compartments.
